title: The Road to Reims
description: June-July 1429. After the victory at Orleans, Joan of Arc must escort the Dauphin Charles through English-held territory to the cathedral at Reims for his coronation. English garrisons at Troyes and Chalons block the route and can be fought or persuaded to surrender. Victory requires the Dauphin reaching Reims cathedral alive; his death means defeat.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID placed as an English garrison commander: Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar died in 1099 and was Castilian, not English, and never fought in Champagne

WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR as the other enemy commander: he died in 1087, 342 years before the march to Reims; the editor offers period-correct English heroes from the Joan of Arc campaign (Sir John Fastolf, Duke of Suffolk) that were avoidable substitutes
English garrison armed with CROSSBOWMAN only: the engine provides the Longbowman, the signature English unit of the Hundred Years' War, so the crossbow-only garrison is an avoidable mismatch
PAVILION_A in the French camp is a decorative Asian/tent-style object rather than European campaign architecture
